result.summary: Independently re-ran npm run lint (exit 0, 0 errors, 4 pre-existing warnings, none touching messages/en.json) and npm run build (exit 0, compiled successfully) - both match TEST-RUNNER's report exactly. AC3/ISSUE-A resolved independently: ran the spec's exact domain-vocabulary script myself against the actual messages/en.json and got Event=9/Chapter=3/Talk=6/Speaker=1/CFP=2/Agenda=0/Check-in=0/Going=1/Watching=0, identical to TEST-RUNNER's 'actual' figures and NOT matching the spec's stated 'Expected' block (16/17/22). Ruled out two alternative explanations for the discrepancy: (1) file drift - git log -- messages/en.json shows only one commit (4f64664) ever wrote the file's content, before the spec commit (631000a), with zero changes since, so the spec author had the exact same file I just checked; (2) wrong-source-file mixup - ran the same script against messages/ru.json and got Event=0/Chapter=0/Talk=0 (mostly Cyrillic), which also does not match 16/17/22, so the spec's numbers were not accidentally computed from ru.json either. The 16/17/22 figures cannot be reconciled with any real script run against any real file on this branch; they are erroneous/fabricated data in the spec's Expected block, not evidence of a REQ-004 content defect. Independently re-verified all 8 named AC3 spot-check values character-for-character (all match), and manually inspected every one of the 22 actual term hits across the file (Event, Chapter, Talk, Speaker, CFP, Going) - no synonym substitution anywhere; 'ongoing' (Doors.door3Tag) and generic 'talk about'/'meetup' usages are correctly non-domain generic English, not vocabulary violations. AC3's real acceptance criterion (verbatim vocabulary, no synonyms) is genuinely satisfied. Every other AC independently re-checked directly against the file/rendered page, not trusted from the report: AC1 (177 keys, empty_en_values=[], 18 identical-value keys, exact match), AC2 (0 Cyrillic matches), AC4 (source values exact match all 8, globals.css:152 .status selector confirmed unconditional text-transform:uppercase, rendered curl output exact match all 8 status spans), AC5a (0 exclamation marks), AC5b (0 emoji matches), AC5c (manually read title/lede/cta values across all 12 sections, confirmed plain functional tone, no slogans). AC6 rendered-page checks re-run against a freshly booted npm run start production server: 6a/6a-control (0 MISSING_MESSAGE/IntlError on /en and /ru), 6b all 4 spot-check strings exact match, 200 status, plus an additional independent check not in the report (raw namespaced-key leakage scan on rendered /en HTML: 0 matches; stray-Cyrillic scan on rendered /en HTML: 0 matches). docs/agents/requirements.yaml REQ-004 entry checked: status=in_progress, which is correct pre-DOC-UPDATER state (not stale - DOC-UPDATER flips it after this PASS). ISSUE-B (browser automation gap) independently reconfirmed via ToolSearch: no Playwright/Puppeteer/browser-automation MCP tool available in this environment. Checked handoffs/orchestrator.log: this is confirmed as the THIRD recurrence (REQ-001a step-04, REQ-003 step-04 and step-05, REQ-004 step-10 and this step-11) across two roles (TEST-RUNNER and RELEASE-VALIDATOR) each independently hitting the identical gap. Notably, the prior RELEASE-VALIDATOR run (step-05, REQ-003) already explicitly recommended escalating this to a system-level issue, but docs/issues/ contains no filed issue for it (only README.md) - the recommendation was never turned into a tracked issue.
